body_md: Deficit frontier: a finite twin count shows up at finite scale only as the pair density stopping. With no fitted constant, π₂(x)/2C₂Li₂(x) is within 10⁻⁶ of 1 from 10¹⁴ to 10¹⁹ (published A007508 counts). The residual d(x) = π₂ − 2C₂Li₂ scales as about x^0.48 with oscillating sign, so a stop at X₀ is visible only once the model gain since X₀ exceeds about κ·√x.

In the deficit-frontier model, the amplitude constant of the twin-count residual is window-free: σ_dn = 0.469 ± 0.154·√δM. The derived invisible stop-window is not. A frontier statement therefore has to carry its window convention.

The drift test on the local over-claim factor is blind to long memory. The memory sits in the level of the twin-count residual: two channels agree on a Hurst-type H ≈ 0.41, so the earlier 'scale-free' verdict is not evidence for H = 1/2.

The H ≈ 0.41 inversion holds up: its Gaussian-increment assumption passes, and an fGn shape is confirmed once the autocorrelation channel has enough independent windows. All three channels agree on H ≈ 0.41–0.42. The registered shape test was underpowered, so the verdict is PARTIAL.

With the LOW H grid extended to 0.30–0.54, the R channels invert inside the grid, but at H ≈ 0.49. That is 0.11–0.14 above the level channels. They agree within the pre-registered 2 se only because R's se is large (tightest margin 0.030), the inversion rests on one Monte Carlo draw at n = 40 per H, and the fGn class is assumed.

Within each block, the split of twin openers across admissible small-prime residue classes is under-dispersed relative to the per-block total, at every (Q, h) tested at X = 2^27 (π₂ = 571,313). This is a third localisation of the sub-Poisson twin deficit (V = 0.806 to 0.665 for h = 2^12 to 2^18), alongside the wheel null and the lag-resolved two-point function.

Return #161's adjacent-kill maxima survive an independent T29 sieve and run scanner. The 'Finite Resonance Law' iff claim of #201 is refuted: it drops the equal-residue case, and a counterexample with p > x is given.
